clue.text: Search youth on return? That's an outrage!

parts.note: to search an area is to scan it

indicators.note: on return asks for the word for youth to be read backwards

parts.note: a youth is a lad

explanation.surface: Someone is shocked that a young person is being searched on coming home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on return' turns LAD into DAL; the question mark and exclamation dress a charade as an outburst.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words name a public disgrace that provokes indignation.

clue.text: Children holding a cleric up must be parted

indicators.note: holding means the word for children wraps around the other piece

parts.note: seed is an old word for offspring or descendants

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the cleric's title is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Rev is the short title of a reverend, a clergyman

explanation.surface: Kids hoisting a vicar into the air are told they must be separated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses REV to VER in this down clue; seed for children is a biblical sense of descendants.
explanation.definitionFit: Severed means cut apart, divided from the rest.

clue.text: Making it clear what's to appear in the newspaper

definitions.meaning: THE is the definite ..., the grammatical word that makes clear which thing is meant

definitions.text: what's to appear in the newspaper
definitions.meaning: a written piece printed in a paper

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is grammatical: a definite article such as 'the' makes plain which noun is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: A grammatical determiner like 'the' is one sense; a piece of journalism is the other.

clue.text: The beauty's limiting factor

parts.note: plays on the saying that beauty is only skin deep: the layer that sets its limit

explanation.surface: A remark about what holds back someone's good looks.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb 'beauty is only skin deep' makes the skin the limit of beauty.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a term for the skin, the deep layer beneath the surface.

clue.text: Count the cash — and with a gloomy look!

parts.note: L stands for pounds sterling, the British money sign
a grave expression is solemn and gloomy

explanation.surface: Someone tallies the money with a sombre face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Count' looks like a verb about money but is a noun: a German nobleman.
explanation.definitionFit: A landgrave was a German noble title, equivalent in rank to a count over a territory.

clue.text: He's in or out — but not far out

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of the words before it are disordered

explanation.surface: Someone wavers between in and out, but stays near.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges HESINOR.
explanation.definitionFit: Inshore means close to the coast rather than far out at sea.

clue.text: The subject of progeny

definitions.meaning: the matter under discussion, the point at stake

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a topic in dispute and, in legal language, a person's offspring.

clue.text: Dope the prime minister is upset to reveal

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'Dope the prime minister is upset to reveal', gives no fodder for SIMPLETON: PM and IS leave LETON with no clue word supplying it; a search found no fuller text.
annotationWithheld.clue: Dope the prime minister is upset to reveal

clue.text: Pacific islands — a canoe may be used to get round one

indicators.note: to get round means the rearranged letters surround the other piece
may be used tells us the letters of a canoe are put to use in a new order

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A traveller paddles around a single Pacific island by canoe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be used' rearranges A CANOE into OCEANA; 'to get round' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Oceania is the collective name for the island groups of the Pacific.

clue.text: The heart of a continental city church

parts.note: Essen is a city in Germany, on the European continent
CE stands for the Church of England

explanation.surface: Describes the core of a church in a European city.
explanation.definitionFit: Essence is the core or most vital part of something.

clue.text: Old serving man and Gallic queen getting in front

indicators.note: getting in means the French word and the queen go inside the word for front

parts.note: the van is the leading part of an army
et is the French word for and
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: An elderly retainer and a French queen push to the front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting in' puts ETER inside VAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A veteran is someone who has served long, especially an ex-serviceman.

clue.text: They add up in the warmer weather!

definitions.meaning: people who sum figures, those who do sums
the hot seasons of the year

explanation.definitionFit: Read as one who sums, the word means calculators; read normally it is the plural of the hot season.

clue.text: About a hundred contend this should be the figure

parts.note: re means about or concerning
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
to tangle with someone is to fight or contend

explanation.surface: Roughly a hundred people argue over what the number should be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'figure' reads as a number but means a geometric shape.
explanation.definitionFit: A rectangle is a four-sided geometric shape with right angles.

clue.text: Material left in French centre

indicators.note: centre takes the middle letters of the word French

explanation.surface: Fabric was left in the middle of France.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle two letters of 'French' are EN.
explanation.definitionFit: Linen is a cloth woven from flax.

clue.text: Trepidation could cause daughter to peruse books

parts.note: to peruse books is to read

explanation.surface: Anxiety might drive a daughter to turn to reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words name fear and apprehension about what may come.

clue.text: To advise against a destructive device needed resolve

parts.note: to deter is to discourage or advise against
a mine is an explosive device

explanation.surface: Persuading people against a bomb needed firm will.
explanation.definitionFit: To resolve and to determine both mean to settle on a decision.

clue.text: Decide a body of soldiers must take in little deserter

indicators.note: must take in means the soldiers' letters surround the other pieces

parts.note: RE stands for the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
a bit is a little
a rat is someone who deserts a cause

explanation.surface: A military unit must decide whether to take back a minor deserter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'must take in' puts BITRAT inside RE, after A.
explanation.definitionFit: To arbitrate is to judge a dispute and settle it.

clue.text: Tree only to be seen around extreme north

indicators.note: to be seen around means the word for only encloses the other letters

parts.note: but can mean only, as in 'but a child'
utter means complete or extreme

explanation.surface: A tree grows only in the far north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be seen around' puts UTTERN inside BUT.
explanation.definitionFit: The butternut is a North American walnut tree.

clue.text: The management all for patient progress

definitions.meaning: the way something is handled or dealt with
medical care given to help a sick person recover

explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both the handling of a matter and medical care given to someone ill.

clue.text: A bishop getting into knots causes delays

indicators.note: getting into means the bishop goes inside the word for knots

parts.note: ties are knots
RR is Right Reverend, a bishop's title

explanation.surface: A bishop tying himself in knots holds everything up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting into' puts ARR inside TIES.
explanation.definitionFit: To tarry is to linger or dawdle, holding things up.

clue.text: Grudging character resisting acknowledgements of indebtedness

parts.note: en is a printer's measure, a character width
V is versus, against
IOUs are notes acknowledging a debt

explanation.surface: A resentful person refuses to accept promissory notes.
explanation.walkthrough: EN is a printing unit the width of a letter n.
explanation.definitionFit: Envious means resentful of another's good fortune, begrudging them it.

clue.text: One of the family is particular about direction

indicators.note: about means the word for particular goes round the direction

parts.note: nice can mean fussy or particular
E is east, a compass direction

explanation.surface: A relative is fussy about which way to go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts E inside NICE.
explanation.definitionFit: A niece is a brother's or sister's daughter, so a relative.

clue.text: Colour deeply when grannie turns awkward

indicators.note: turns awkward means the letters of grannie are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone's face goes deep red when granny gets difficult.
explanation.definitionFit: To engrain is to dye fast, working colour deep into fibres.

clue.text: Anything but mean

parts.note: mean here is the average, so its opposite is something at the far end of a range

explanation.surface: Describing someone very generous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mean' suggests stingy, but it is the statistical average.
explanation.definitionFit: Extreme means at the furthest point, as far from the middle as possible.

clue.text: A vagrant involved in some controversy

indicators.note: involved in some means the letters sit inside the clue word controversy

explanation.surface: A tramp gets caught up in a dispute.
explanation.definitionFit: A rover is a wanderer with no fixed home.

clue.text: Military command looks good

parts.note: eyes as a verb means looks at
right means correct or good

explanation.surface: A parade order appears satisfactory.
explanation.definitionFit: A drill order to turn the head to the right in salute.

clue.text: Breakfasted soundly at a reasonable time

indicators.note: soundly signals that the word is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: breakfasted means ate

explanation.surface: Someone had a good breakfast at a sensible hour.
explanation.definitionFit: Eight o'clock is a sensible hour, for instance for breakfast.

clue.text: One within rights as a sportsman

indicators.note: within means the one sits inside the rights

parts.note: R is right, so two are rights
an ace is a one in cards

explanation.surface: Someone is within their rights as an athlete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'within' puts ACE between the two Rs.
explanation.definitionFit: A racer is someone who competes in races.

clue.text: Pressing for neatness

parts.note: pressing reads as urgent, but here means flattening clothes to look tidy

explanation.surface: An urgent demand for tidiness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pressing' looks like urgent; it is the act of smoothing clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Ironing smooths creases from clothes with a hot iron.

clue.text: Offering tasteless stuff in attractive wrapping, wink

indicators.note: wrapping means the word for attractive goes round the other piece

parts.note: nice means pleasant or attractive
tat is cheap tasteless goods

explanation.surface: A seller offers cheap junk in pretty packaging with a knowing wink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Offering' is only a link; 'wrapping' signals the container, and nictate is a rare formal word for wink.
explanation.definitionFit: To nictate is to blink or wink.

clue.text: American page in school — fancy!

indicators.note: in means the American and page go inside the school

parts.note: a school of thought is a sect
US is the United States

explanation.surface: An American pageboy at school catches someone's eye.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts USP inside SECT.
explanation.definitionFit: To suspect is to imagine or think likely, to fancy.

clue.text: A man can start even following recent reform

indicators.note: following places the first letter after the rearranged word
reform means the letters of recent are made over in a new order
start takes the first letter of even

explanation.surface: Someone can make a fresh start after a recent change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reform' rearranges RECENT into TERENC; 'start' gives E from 'even'.
explanation.definitionFit: Terence is a man's first name.
